title: Minimum Number of Moves to Make Palindrome
statement:
You are given a string `s` made of lowercase English letters. In one **move** you may choose any two **adjacent** characters and swap them.

Return the minimum number of moves needed to turn `s` into a palindrome. The input is guaranteed to be convertible into a palindrome by some sequence of adjacent swaps (equivalently, at most one letter occurs an odd number of times).

This problem appeared as a "minimum adjacent swaps to make a string a palindrome" question in an online assessment.
input_format: A single line containing the string `s`.
output_format: Print a single integer: the minimum number of adjacent swaps.
constraints: `s` can be rearranged into a palindrome

examples.explanation: Swap the first two characters: `abcab` → `bacab`, which is a palindrome. It is not already a palindrome, so at least one move is needed.
`aabcb` → `abacb` → `baacb` → `bacab`. Three swaps reach the palindrome `bacab`, and no sequence of two swaps does.
The string is already a palindrome.

hints: Look at the last character. It must be mirrored by an equal character at the front half. Which occurrence is cheapest to bring to the front?
Greedily take the first occurrence of the last character: moving it to index 0 costs exactly its index in swaps. Then delete both ends and repeat on the shorter string.
If the last character occurs only once in what remains, it is the middle character of the final palindrome. Moving it to the center costs `len // 2` swaps; remove it and continue.
reference:
import sys

def main():
    s = list(sys.stdin.readline().strip())
    res = 0
    while len(s) > 1:
        i = s.index(s[-1])
        if i == len(s) - 1:
            res += len(s) // 2
            s.pop()
        else:
            res += i
            s.pop()
            s.pop(i)
    print(res)

main()
